subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Seals and Shields: Keeping Dirt Out
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Seals and Shields: Keeping Dirt Out.

hook.text: A single grain of sand can wreck a bearing. Seals keep dirt out.

buildup.text: Shields are metal covers with a gap. Seals are rubber and make contact.

discovery.text: Seals block dirt better but add drag. Shields allow higher speed.

twist.text: A worn seal lets moisture in. Rust then kills the bearing from inside.

climax.text: Sealed bearings come pre-greased for life. Open ones need oil feeds.

punchline.text: Keep the dirt out and the bearing keeps spinning.

quiz.question: What is the trade-off between seals and shields?
options: Seals block dirt better but add drag; shields allow higher speed
Seals are cheaper but wear faster; shields are pricier but last longer
Seals work only with oil; shields work only with grease
